## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Todeyyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 410) is a verse hagiography preserved in the Therāpadāna section of the Khuddaka Nikāya, recording the spiritual biography and meritorious past deeds of the elder Todeyya [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
According to SuttaCentral, the text is cross-referenced with or mentioned in the *Mahājanakajātaka* (Ja 539), the *Soṇakajātaka* (Ja 529), and neighboring apadāna accounts, specifically the *Hemakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 409) and *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, finding 230 matches across 26 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse correspondences occur with the two volumes of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), as well as related poems in the *Therāpadāna* including the *Hemakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 409, sharing §40.1–44.4), *Udenattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 412), *Ajitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 402), and *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413) [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares significant verse material with major Jātaka compositions, aligning passages with the *Mahājanakajātaka* (Ja 539, §16.2–19.3) and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547, §16.2–19.2) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also identifies low-scoring machine alignments with diverse Mahāyāna and Āgama texts in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan—such as the *Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha*, *Ajitasenavyākaraṇa*, the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), and the Tibetan *Samādhirājasūtra* (D 127)—though these reflect formulaic resemblances rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
